title: Under strict rule until sixteen, then playing in the joints
summary: He had to report straight home until about sixteen, then was allowed to play with adults in local joints; Bob Carroll came out of there too, and he credits Mrs. Allen for Louisville's musicians.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was up at some age when I was ruled with an iron hand, you know. When I left Sunday school I had to come straight home, you know. Sure. You'd come home and let them know you're there. You didn't hang around the corner or anything. This happened till I got up to around 16 years old.

Sure. Yeah, you tell them where you are, you know. And then they kind of let me loose and let me play with some of the adults around town, in the joints, you know, which is good for you. And another one that played in there was Bob Carroll. Do you remember him?
He played with Teddy Hill. I remember quite a few of those guys, yeah.
Well, Louisville was really quite a place for a guy who was coming up.
Yeah, a lot of music around there.
Well, do you think that it had a lot to do with that, that so many guys got a foundation?

Well, them guys coming out of there, they would have never gotten out of there. They would never have gotten into music or nothing, unless you had a setup like that. As I say, this woman was so wonderful.
